title: replace: compiled and string regex spellings must take the same path and be tested together
answers: replace regex=True vs re.compile behave differently
what tests to add when changing regex replace for arrow strings
replace with regex upcasts arrow string column to object
Categorical replace regex new category raises TypeError
body:
Any spelling of the same pattern must behave the same: `regex={pat: v}`, `to_replace=pat, regex=True`, `to_replace=[re.compile(pat)], value=[v], regex=True`, and bare `to_replace=re.compile(pat)`. This covers the upcast to object when an arrow string column can't hold the replacement (GH-70458). The compiled list/dict forms go through replace_list and reach the same Block._replace_regex guard.
Tests parametrize over all four spellings: pandas/tests/series/methods/test_replace.py (test_replace_compiled_regex_arrow_dtype, test_replace_regex_non_string_arrow_dtype with `compile_pattern`) and pandas/tests/arrays/categorical/test_replace.py (…_arrow_strings variants). For a Categorical, a replacement that matches an existing category works, and a new category raises `TypeError: Cannot setitem on a Categorical with a new category`.
When a test checks that the original was not mutated, compare against a copy explicitly. Asserting the result alone passes even after mutation, because `^a` no longer matches substituted values. Also cover inplace=True with a view (`ser[:]`), which now reaches ArrowExtensionArray.__setitem__.
Known open inconsistency: non-regex `ser.replace("a", 1)` on arrow strings still raises instead of upcasting.
applies: Changes to replace/regex handling for string, arrow and categorical dtypes and their tests
